'''Nikku Madhusudhan''' is an [[Indian British]] [[astronomer]] and [[professor]] of [[astrophysics]] and Exoplanetary Science at the [[Institute of Astronomy, Cambridge|Institute of Astronomy]], [[University of Cambridge]]. He is credited with developing an improved technique of atmospheric retrieval to infer the compositions of [[exoplanet]]s, and with coining the term "[[hycean planet]]" to describe a theorised class of planet which hosts a liquid water ocean beneath a hydrogen-rich atmosphere.

==Biography==
Madhusudhan obtained a B.Tech. at [[Indian Institute of Technology (BHU) Varanasi]] before pursuing a M.S. and [[PhD|Ph.D.]] at [[MIT]]. His doctoral advisor was [[Sara Seager]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.saraseager.com/exoplanet-atmospheres/|title=Exoplanet Atmospheres - Sara Seager|publisher=saraseager.com}}</ref>

During his PhD, Madhusudhan developed an improved method for atmospheric retrieval, the process of inferring the composition and temperature structure of exoplanet atmospheres from their observed spectra.<ref name="madhusudhan2009" /> In 2012, Madhusudhan showed that the mass and radius of the [[super-Earth]] [[55 Cancri e]] was consistent with a [[carbon]]-rich interior.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/121011-diamond-planet-space-solar-system-astronomy-science|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210226035333/https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/121011-diamond-planet-space-solar-system-astronomy-science|url-status=dead|archive-date=26 February 2021|title=Diamond Planet Found - Part of a "Whole New Class?"|publisher=nationalgeographic.com}}</ref> In 2014, he led a team which obtained high-precision measurements of the atmospheric water abundances of three [[hot Jupiter]]s, finding less water than would be expected given planet formation models at the time.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hubblesite.org/contents/news-releases/2014/news-2014-36.html|title=Hubble Finds Three Surprisingly Dry Exoplanets|publisher=hubblesite.org}}</ref>

In 2020, Madhusudhan led a team who studied the interior and atmosphere of the [[mini-Neptune]] exoplanet [[K2-18b]].<ref name="madhusudhan2020" /> They found that in certain cases, liquid water may exist on the planet's surface, albeit at temperatures and pressures higher than [[Standard temperature and pressure|STP]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://edition.cnn.com/2020/02/26/world/k218b-exoplanet-water-habitable-scn/index.html|title=Potentially habitable exoplanet could broaden the search for life beyond Earth|publisher=cnn.com}}</ref>
